messages:
incident-bot: Pagerduty alert triggered — reserved pool resv-westus-3 CPU/GPU pressure. metric: reserved_gpu_utilization=99%, queue_length=820, p90_latency_tokens=1.8s. severity: P1. https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/resv-westus-3
oncall-maria: acknowledging. I'm pulling metrics and will join bridge in 2m. Pager pinned. :thumbsup:
eng-sre-ben: looking at autoscaler logs — scale attempt failed at 2026-05-12T01:05:12Z with error 'scale-limit-reached: max_reserved_nodes=12' for resv-westus-3. Recent config shows max_reserved_nodes=12 and min=4. Queue growth since 00:45 UTC, steady.
eng-runtime-jun: adding context — we've seen this pattern when a large reserved tenant opens many concurrent sessions (KV cache heavy). Which tenant is top?
eng-sre-ben: top consumer by GPU time: tenant: asclepius-inc (tenant_id: t-9891), 54% of pool. noise pattern: many short live sessions from their inference playground.
cs-alyssa: asclepius reported latency spikes ~00:50 UTC and some 503s. They're on an enterprise reserved plan (resv-westus-3). They're on slack channel with their SE, pinged them already.
infra-kavita: quick check — cloud quota prevents adding more reserved nodes: account quota for region-westus reserved gpus = 16, current reserved used = 16, limit set by billing account.
oncall-maria: action list: 1) throttle noisy tenant concurrency; 2) attempt temporary burst to shared pool or fallback model routing; 3) escalate quota to cloud/billing if needed. Who can run tenant throttle?
eng-runtime-jun: I can push a soft-concurrency limit for t-9891 via our routing rules: 
```
redwood-admin tenants set-concurrency --tenant t-9891 --max-concurrent 6 --reason "incident: noisy sessions"
```
I'll prep the command. Need approval from platform-esc for any customer-facing throttles?
platform-esc: temporary throttles are allowed per SLO emergency policy but must be communicated. Please include cs and record change in incident ticket.
eng-sre-ben: running a dry-check on routing change effects...
eng-runtime-jun: applied soft throttle: t-9891 max-concurrent=6. Confirmed in router logs: dropped new session attempts for that tenant ~00:07:20 after change. Expected to reduce queue.
eng-sre-ben: CPU/GPU queue length dropped from 820 -> 260 in 90s. p90 latency trending down. Good immediate impact.
incident-bot: Deploy job #deploy-789 started by eng-runtime-jun (routing change). CI checks passed.
infra-kavita: still seeing sustained utilization 94% on reserved GPUs. Autoscaler still at max_reserved_nodes=12. Request to cloud quota is in progress (ticket #BILL-4721). Estimated SLA for quota bump 6-8h unless expedited.
cs-alyssa: letting Asclepius SE know we applied a temporary throttle. They asked for any mitigation to avoid user impact. We offered canary reroute to hosted pool with degraded model (latency slightly higher, cost higher but availability).
eng-runtime-jun: starting canary reroute for non-authenticated playground traffic from t-9891 to hosted-fallback-1: tag-based traffic split 10% -> hosted-fallback-1. Command:
```
redwood-admin routing split --from-tenant t-9891 --match "playground:true" --percent 10 --to hosted-fallback-1
```
Applied. Monitoring.
eng-sre-ben: metrics: queue 260 -> 110 in 5 min after throttles + 10% reroute. No new 503s from Asclepius. p95 tokens latency down to 1.1s.
oncall-maria: what's longer-term fix while quota ticket pending? Can we evict idle sessions from noisy tenant?
platform-esc: eviction is allowed if idle > 10m and tenant over threshold >50% of pool. Ben, can we run eviction script? Must coordinate with CS.
eng-sre-ben: prepping eviction targeting sessions flagged as 'playground' and idle>5m to be conservative. Script:
```
redwood-admin sessions evict --tenant t-9891 --filter "playground:true and idle>5m" --dry-run
```
Dry-run shows ~420 sessions eligible, would free ~6 GPUs equivalent. Need CS sign-off before executing.
cs-alyssa: please hold dry-run results. I'll message Asclepius SE right now and request permission for emergency eviction; if they deny, we'll escalate to legal/ops per policy.
pagerduty-bot: reminder: incident P1 has been active for 18 minutes. Next on-call rotation: infra-kavita.
cs-alyssa: SE replied — they authorize emergency eviction for non-auth playground sessions. Proceed.
eng-sre-ben: executing eviction now.
eng-sre-ben: eviction completed: 412 sessions terminated, freed ~5.8 GPU equivalents. reserved GPU utilization down to 78%. queue length now 32.
eng-runtime-jun: confirming route policies and caches — KV cache warmed for production traffic. No errors observed from core app.
oncall-maria: great work. Summarize customer impact: Asclepius saw degraded playground availability during window 00:45-01:10 UTC, some 503s; production inference for their primary workloads unaffected. CS to follow up with post-incident note.
platform-esc: create follow-up action items: 1) request quota bump (BILL-4721) escalate to cloud partner; 2) evaluate reservation sizing guidance and enforce tenant-level concurrency defaults; 3) add a safeguard in autoscaler to allow temporary soft-burst to shared pool; 4) add better alerting segmentation by tenant. Assign owners.
eng-runtime-jun: created ticket INF-9987 for postmortem and playbook updates.
oncall-maria: closing bridge in 10m unless further regressions. Please add logs & commands to the incident ticket.
eng-sre-ben: adding command outputs and eviction audit to INF-9987.
cs-alyssa: I've informed Asclepius that we applied throttles and eviction; they'll prepare a user-facing note.
incident-bot: Incident P1 resolved? status: mitigated — reserved pool utilization under threshold. Please update incident record and set postmortem owner.
eng-sre-ben: marking incident mitigated. Postmortem owner: eng-sre-ben.
eng-runtime-jun: agreed. Follow-up to include automated tenant-level burst protection and explicit max_reserved_nodes review.
platform-esc: will take the quota escalation and policy changes as action items.
oncall-maria: thanks all. Good recovery. We'll ping if anything else. :pray:
